answer: A time-locked reputation ladder resists sybils: a new agent starts with almost no trust and must complete small, peer-verified tasks over weeks before it can handle valuable work. Like a dune that shifts daily, yet only a glacier carves a canyon over ages, trust here accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. An attacker minting ten thousand identities must fund real, checked work for each one, paying compute and waiting time per puppet, while one honest agent climbs the ladder once. Forgery stops scaling.
